members.doc: Pops the current save stack, if there is anything to pop. Otherwise, does nothing.

members.name: restoreToCount
members.doc: Restores the save stack to a previous level as might be obtained from getSaveCount. If count is less than 1, the stack is restored to its initial state. If count is greater than the current getSaveCount then nothing happens.

members.name: getSaveCount
members.doc: Returns the number of items on the save stack, including the initial state. This means it returns 1 for a clean canvas, and that each call to save and saveLayer increments it, and that each matching call to restore decrements it.

members.doc: Add a translation to the current transform, shifting the coordinate space horizontally by the first argument and vertically by the second argument.

members.name: scale
members.doc: Add an axis-aligned scale to the current transform, scaling by the first argument in the horizontal direction and the second in the vertical direction.

members.name: rotate
members.doc: Add a rotation to the current transform. The argument is in radians clockwise.

members.name: skew
members.doc: Add an axis-aligned skew to the current transform, with the first argument being the horizontal skew in rise over run units clockwise around the origin, and the second argument being the vertical skew in rise over run units clockwise around the origin.

members.name: transform
members.doc: Multiply the current transform by the specified 4⨉4 transformation matrix specified as a list of values in column-major order.

members.doc: Returns the current transform including the combined result of all transform methods executed since the creation of this Canvas object, and respecting the save/restore history.

declarations.name: CupertinoLinearActivityIndicator
declarations.doc: An iOS-style linear activity indicator.

constructors.doc: Creates a linear iOS-style activity indicator.

members.name: progress
members.doc: The current progress of the linear activity indicator.

members.name: height
members.doc: The height of the line used to draw the linear activity indicator.

members.name: color
members.doc: The color of the progress bar.

declarations.name: CupertinoListSection
declarations.doc: An iOS-style list section.

constructors.doc: Creates a section that mimics standard iOS forms.

constructors.name: insetGrouped
constructors.doc: Creates a section that mimics standard "Inset Grouped" iOS list section.

members.name: type
members.doc: The type of list section, either base or inset grouped.

members.name: header
members.doc: Sets the form section header. The section header lies above the children rows. Usually a Text widget.

members.name: footer
members.doc: Sets the form section footer. The section footer lies below the children rows. Usually a Text widget.

members.name: margin
members.doc: Margin around the content area of the section encapsulating children.

members.name: children
members.doc: The list of rows in the section. Usually a list of CupertinoListTiles.

members.name: decoration
members.doc: Sets the decoration around children.

members.name: backgroundColor
members.doc: Sets the background color behind the section.

members.name: dividerMargin
members.doc: The starting offset of a margin between two list tiles.

members.name: additionalDividerMargin
members.doc: Additional starting inset of the divider used between rows. This is used when adding a leading icon to children and a divider should start at the text inset instead of the icon.

members.name: topMargin
members.doc: Margin above the list section. Only used in edge-to-edge variant and it matches iOS style by default.

members.name: separatorColor
members.doc: Sets the color for the dividers between rows, and borders on top and bottom of the rows.

declarations.name: CupertinoListSectionType
declarations.doc: Denotes what type of the list section a CupertinoListSection is.

declarations.name: CupertinoListTile
declarations.doc: An iOS-style list tile.

constructors.doc: Creates an edge-to-edge iOS-style list tile like the tiles in iOS Settings app.

constructors.name: notched
constructors.doc: Creates a notched iOS-style list tile like the tiles in iOS Notes app or Reminders app.

members.name: title
members.doc: A title is used to convey the central information. Usually a Text.

members.name: subtitle
members.doc: A subtitle is used to display additional information. It is located below title. Usually a Text widget.

members.name: additionalInfo
members.doc: Similar to subtitle, an additionalInfo is used to display additional information. However, instead of being displayed below title, it is displayed on the right, before trailing. Usually a Text widget.

members.name: leading
members.doc: A widget displayed at the start of the CupertinoListTile. This is typically an `Icon` or an `Image`.

members.name: trailing
members.doc: A widget displayed at the end of the CupertinoListTile. This is usually a right chevron icon (e.g. `CupertinoListTileChevron`), or an `Icon`.

members.name: onTap
members.doc: The onTap function is called when a user taps on CupertinoListTile. If left `null`, the CupertinoListTile will not react on taps.

members.name: backgroundColor
members.doc: The backgroundColor of the tile in normal state. Once the tile is tapped, the background color switches to backgroundColorActivated. It is set to match the iOS look by default.

members.name: backgroundColorActivated
members.doc: The backgroundColorActivated is the background color of the tile after the tile was tapped. It is set to match the iOS look by default.

members.name: padding
members.doc: Padding of the content inside CupertinoListTile.

members.name: leadingSize
members.doc: The leadingSize is used to constrain the width and height of leading widget.

members.name: leadingToTitle
members.doc: The horizontal space between leading widget and title.

declarations.name: CupertinoListTileChevron
declarations.doc: A typical iOS trailing widget used to denote that a `CupertinoListTile` is a button with an action.

constructors.doc: Creates a typical widget used to denote that a `CupertinoListTile` is a button with action.

declarations.name: CupertinoLocalizations
declarations.doc: Defines the localized resource values used by the Cupertino widgets.

members.name: datePickerDateOrder
members.doc: The order of the date elements that will be shown in CupertinoDatePicker.

members.name: datePickerDateTimeOrder
members.doc: The order of the time elements that will be shown in CupertinoDatePicker.

members.name: anteMeridiemAbbreviation
members.doc: The abbreviation for ante meridiem (before noon) shown in the time picker.

members.name: postMeridiemAbbreviation
members.doc: The abbreviation for post meridiem (after noon) shown in the time picker.

members.name: todayLabel
members.doc: Label shown in date pickers when the date is today.

members.name: alertDialogLabel
members.doc: The term used by the system to announce dialog alerts.

members.name: timerPickerHourLabels
members.doc: All possible hour labels that appears next to the hour picker in CupertinoTimerPicker

members.name: timerPickerMinuteLabels
members.doc: All possible minute labels that appears next to the minute picker in CupertinoTimerPicker

members.name: timerPickerSecondLabels
members.doc: All possible second labels that appears next to the second picker in CupertinoTimerPicker

members.name: cutButtonLabel
members.doc: The term used for cutting.

members.name: copyButtonLabel
members.doc: The term used for copying.

members.name: pasteButtonLabel
members.doc: The term used for pasting.

members.name: clearButtonLabel
members.doc: The term used for clearing a field.

members.name: noSpellCheckReplacementsLabel
members.doc: Label that appears in the Cupertino toolbar when the spell checker couldn't find any replacements for the current word.

members.name: selectAllButtonLabel
members.doc: The term used for selecting everything.

members.name: lookUpButtonLabel
members.doc: The term used for looking up a selection.

members.name: searchWebButtonLabel
members.doc: The term used for launching a web search on a selection.

members.name: shareButtonLabel
members.doc: The term used for launching a web search on a selection.

members.name: searchTextFieldPlaceholderLabel
members.doc: The default placeholder used in CupertinoSearchTextField.

members.name: modalBarrierDismissLabel
members.doc: Label read out by accessibility tools (VoiceOver) for a modal barrier to indicate that a tap dismisses the barrier.

members.name: menuDismissLabel

members.doc: A linear animation curve.

members.doc: A curve where the rate of change starts out quickly and then decelerates; an upside-down `f(t) = t²` parabola.

members.doc: A curve that is very steep and linear at the beginning, but quickly flattens out and very slowly eases in.

members.doc: A curve that starts slowly, speeds up very quickly, and then ends slowly.

members.doc: A cubic animation curve that speeds up quickly and ends slowly.

members.doc: A cubic animation curve that starts slowly and ends quickly.

members.name: easeInToLinear
members.doc: A cubic animation curve that starts slowly and ends linearly.

members.name: easeInSine
members.doc: A cubic animation curve that starts slowly and ends quickly. This is similar to Curves.easeIn, but with sinusoidal easing for a slightly less abrupt beginning and end. Nonetheless, the result is quite gentle and is hard to distinguish from Curves.linear at a glance.

members.name: easeInQuad
members.doc: A cubic animation curve that starts slowly and ends quickly. Based on a quadratic equation where `f(t) = t²`, this is effectively the inverse of Curves.decelerate.

members.name: easeInCubic
members.doc: A cubic animation curve that starts slowly and ends quickly. This curve is based on a cubic equation where `f(t) = t³`. The result is a safe sweet spot when choosing a curve for widgets animating off the viewport.

members.name: easeInQuart
members.doc: A cubic animation curve that starts slowly and ends quickly. This curve is based on a quartic equation where `f(t) = t⁴`.

members.name: easeInQuint
members.doc: A cubic animation curve that starts slowly and ends quickly. This curve is based on a quintic equation where `f(t) = t⁵`.

members.name: easeInExpo
members.doc: A cubic animation curve that starts slowly and ends quickly. This curve is based on an exponential equation where `f(t) = 2¹⁰⁽ᵗ⁻¹⁾`.

members.name: easeInCirc
members.doc: A cubic animation curve that starts slowly and ends quickly. This curve is effectively the bottom-right quarter of a circle.

members.name: easeInBack
members.doc: A cubic animation curve that starts slowly and ends quickly. This curve is similar to Curves.elasticIn in that it overshoots its bounds before reaching its end. Instead of repeated swinging motions before ascending, though, this curve overshoots once, then continues to ascend.

members.name: easeOut
members.doc: A cubic animation curve that starts quickly and ends slowly.

members.name: linearToEaseOut
members.doc: A cubic animation curve that starts linearly and ends slowly.

members.name: easeOutSine
members.doc: A cubic animation curve that starts quickly and ends slowly. This is similar to Curves.easeOut, but with sinusoidal easing for a slightly less abrupt beginning and end. Nonetheless, the result is quite gentle and is hard to distinguish from Curves.linear at a glance.

members.name: easeOutQuad

members.name: easeOutCubic
members.doc: A cubic animation curve that starts quickly and ends slowly. This curve is a flipped version of Curves.easeInCubic.

members.name: easeOutQuint
members.doc: A cubic animation curve that starts quickly and ends slowly. This curve is a flipped version of Curves.easeInQuint.

members.name: easeOutExpo
members.doc: A cubic animation curve that starts quickly and ends slowly. This curve is a flipped version of Curves.easeInExpo. Using this curve can give your animations extra flare, but a longer duration may need to be used to compensate for the steepness of the curve.

members.name: easeOutCirc
members.doc: A cubic animation curve that starts quickly and ends slowly. This curve is effectively the top-left quarter of a circle.

members.name: easeOutBack
members.doc: A cubic animation curve that starts quickly and ends slowly. This curve is similar to Curves.elasticOut in that it overshoots its bounds before reaching its end. Instead of repeated swinging motions after ascending, though, this curve only overshoots once.

members.name: easeInOut
members.doc: A cubic animation curve that starts slowly, speeds up, and then ends slowly.

members.name: easeInOutSine
members.doc: A cubic animation curve that starts slowly, speeds up, and then ends slowly. This is similar to Curves.easeInOut, but with sinusoidal easing for a slightly less abrupt beginning and end.

members.name: easeInOutQuad
members.doc: A cubic animation curve that starts slowly, speeds up, and then ends slowly. This curve can be imagined as Curves.easeInQuad as the first half, and Curves.easeOutQuad as the second.

members.name: easeInOutQuart

declarations.name: HSLColor
declarations.doc: A color represented using alpha, hue, saturation, and lightness.

constructors.name: fromAHSL
constructors.doc: Creates a color.

constructors.name: fromColor
constructors.doc: Creates an HSLColor from an RGB Color.

members.name: alpha
members.doc: Alpha, from 0.0 to 1.0. The describes the transparency of the color. A value of 0.0 is fully transparent, and 1.0 is fully opaque.

members.name: hue
members.doc: Hue, from 0.0 to 360.0. Describes which color of the spectrum is represented. A value of 0.0 represents red, as does 360.0. Values in between go through all the hues representable in RGB. You can think of this as selecting which color filter is placed over a light.

members.name: saturation
members.doc: Saturation, from 0.0 to 1.0. This describes how colorful the color is. 0.0 implies a shade of grey (i.e. no pigment), and 1.0 implies a color as vibrant as that hue gets. You can think of this as the purity of the color filter over the light.

members.name: lightness
members.doc: Lightness, from 0.0 to 1.0. The lightness of a color describes how bright a color is.

members.name: withAlpha
members.doc: Returns a copy of this color with the alpha parameter replaced with the given value.

members.name: withHue
members.doc: Returns a copy of this color with the hue parameter replaced with the given value.

members.name: withSaturation
members.doc: Returns a copy of this color with the saturation parameter replaced with the given value.

members.name: withLightness
members.doc: Returns a copy of this color with the lightness parameter replaced with the given value.

members.name: toColor
members.doc: Returns this HSL color in RGB.

members.name: lerp
members.doc: Linearly interpolate between two HSLColors.

members.doc: Hue, from 0.0 to 360.0. Describes which color of the spectrum is represented. A value of 0.0 represents red, as does 360.0. Values in between go through all the hues representable in RGB. You can think of this as selecting which pigment will be added to a color.

members.name: saturation

members.doc: Value, from 0.0 to 1.0. The "value" of a color that, in this context, describes how bright a color is. A value of 0.0 indicates black, and 1.0 indicates full intensity color. You can think of this as the equivalent of removing black from the color as value increases.

declarations.name: Icon

members.name: icon
members.doc: The icon to display. The available icons are described in Icons.

members.name: size
members.doc: The size of the icon in logical pixels.

members.name: fill
members.doc: The fill for drawing the icon.

members.name: weight
members.doc: The stroke weight for drawing the icon.

members.name: grade
members.doc: The grade (granular stroke weight) for drawing the icon.

members.name: opticalSize
members.doc: The optical size for drawing the icon.

members.name: color
members.doc: The color to use when drawing the icon.

members.name: shadows
members.doc: A list of Shadows that will be painted underneath the icon.

members.name: semanticLabel
members.doc: Semantic label for the icon.

members.name: textDirection
members.doc: The text direction to use for rendering the icon.

members.name: applyTextScaling
members.doc: Whether to scale the size of this widget using the ambient MediaQuery's TextScaler.

members.name: blendMode
members.doc: The BlendMode to apply to the foreground of the icon.

members.name: fontWeight
members.doc: The typeface thickness to use when painting the text (e.g., bold).

declarations.name: IconButton
declarations.doc: A Material Design icon button.

constructors.doc: Creates an icon button.

constructors.name: filled
constructors.doc: Create a filled variant of IconButton.

constructors.name: filledTonal
constructors.doc: Create a filled tonal variant of IconButton.

constructors.name: outlined
constructors.doc: Create an outlined variant of IconButton.

members.name: iconSize
members.doc: The size of the icon inside the button.

members.name: visualDensity
members.doc: Defines how compact the icon button's layout will be.

members.name: padding
members.doc: The padding around the button's icon. The entire padded icon will react to input gestures.

members.name: alignment
members.doc: Defines how the icon is positioned within the IconButton.

members.name: splashRadius
members.doc: The splash radius.

members.name: icon
members.doc: The icon to display inside the button.

members.name: focusColor
members.doc: The color for the button when it has the input focus.

members.name: hoverColor
members.doc: The color for the button when a pointer is hovering over it.

members.name: color
members.doc: The color to use for the icon inside the button, if the icon is enabled. Defaults to leaving this up to the icon widget.

members.name: splashColor
members.doc: The primary color of the button when the button is in the down (pressed) state. The splash is represented as a circular overlay that appears above the highlightColor overlay.

members.name: highlightColor
members.doc: The secondary color of the button when the button is in the down (pressed) state.

members.name: disabledColor
members.doc: The color to use for the icon inside the button, if the icon is disabled. Defaults to the ThemeData.disabledColor of the current Theme.

members.name: onPressed
members.doc: The callback that is called when the button is tapped or otherwise activated.

members.name: onHover
members.doc: The callback that is called when the button is hovered.

members.name: onLongPress
members.doc: The callback that is called when the button is long-pressed.

members.name: tooltip
members.doc: Text that describes the action that will occur when the button is pressed.

members.name: enableFeedback
members.doc: Whether detected gestures should provide acoustic and/or haptic feedback.

members.name: constraints
members.doc: Optional size constraints for the button.

members.name: style
members.doc: Customizes this button's appearance.

members.name: isSelected
members.doc: The optional selection state of the icon button.

members.name: selectedIcon
members.doc: The icon to display inside the button when isSelected is true. This property can be null. The original icon will be used for both selected and unselected status if it is null.

members.name: styleFrom
members.doc: A static convenience method that constructs an icon button ButtonStyle given simple values. This method is only used for Material 3.

members.name: opticalSize
members.doc: The default for Icon.opticalSize.

members.name: color
members.doc: The default for Icon.color.

members.name: shadows
members.doc: The default for Icon.shadows.

members.name: applyTextScaling

members.name: isConcrete
members.doc: Whether all the properties (except shadows) of this object are non-null.

members.name: opacity
members.doc: An opacity to apply to both explicit and default icon colors.

members.name: copyWith
members.doc: Creates a copy of this icon theme but with the given fields replaced with the new values.

members.name: merge
members.doc: Returns a new icon theme that matches this icon theme but with some values replaced by the non-null parameters of the given icon theme. If the given icon theme is null, returns this icon theme.

members.doc: Called by IconTheme.of to convert this instance to an IconThemeData that fits the given BuildContext.

members.doc: Linearly interpolate between two icon theme data objects.

members.name: shouldReload
members.doc: Returns true if the resources for this delegate should be loaded again by calling the load method.

declarations.name: LocalizationsResolver
declarations.doc: A helper class used to manage localization resolution.

constructors.doc: Creates a LocalizationsResolver that determines the best-fit locale from the set of supportedLocales.

members.name: locale
members.doc: The currently resolved Locale based on the current platform locale and the provided set of supportedLocales.

members.name: update
members.doc: Replace one or more of the properties used for localization resolution and re-resolve the locale.

declarations.name: LockState
declarations.doc: Determines how the state of a lock key is used to accept a shortcut.

declarations.name: LogicalKeySet
declarations.doc: A set of LogicalKeyboardKeys that can be used as the keys in a map.

constructors.doc: A constructor for making a LogicalKeySet of up to four keys.

constructors.name: fromSet
constructors.doc: Create a LogicalKeySet from a set of LogicalKeyboardKeys.

declarations.name: LogicalKeyboardKey
declarations.doc: A class with static values that describe the keys that are returned from RawKeyEvent.logicalKey.

constructors.doc: Creates a new LogicalKeyboardKey object for a key ID.

members.doc: Starts a new sub-path at the given offset from the current point.

members.name: lineTo
members.doc: Adds a straight line segment from the current point to the given point.

members.name: relativeLineTo
members.doc: Adds a straight line segment from the current point to the point at the given offset from the current point.

members.name: quadraticBezierTo
members.doc: Adds a quadratic bezier segment that curves from the current point to the given point (x2,y2), using the control point (x1,y1).

members.name: relativeQuadraticBezierTo
members.doc: Adds a quadratic bezier segment that curves from the current point to the point at the offset (x2,y2) from the current point, using the control point at the offset (x1,y1) from the current point.

members.name: cubicTo
members.doc: Adds a cubic bezier segment that curves from the current point to the given point (x3,y3), using the control points (x1,y1) and (x2,y2).

members.name: relativeCubicTo
members.doc: Adds a cubic bezier segment that curves from the current point to the point at the offset (x3,y3) from the current point, using the control points at the offsets (x1,y1) and (x2,y2) from the current point.

members.name: conicTo
members.doc: Adds a bezier segment that curves from the current point to the given point (x2,y2), using the control points (x1,y1) and the weight w.

members.name: relativeConicTo
members.doc: Adds a bezier segment that curves from the current point to the point at the offset (x2,y2) from the current point, using the control point at the offset (x1,y1) from the current point and the weight w.

members.name: arcTo
members.doc: If the `forceMoveTo` argument is false, adds a straight line segment and an arc segment.

members.name: arcToPoint
members.doc: Appends up to four conic curves weighted to describe an oval of `radius` and rotated by `rotation` (measured in degrees and clockwise).

members.name: relativeArcToPoint
members.doc: Appends up to four conic curves weighted to describe an oval of `radius` and rotated by `rotation` (measured in degrees and clockwise).

members.name: addRect
members.doc: Adds a new sub-path that consists of four lines that outline the given rectangle.

members.name: addOval
members.doc: Adds a new sub-path that consists of a curve that forms the ellipse that fills the given rectangle.

members.name: addArc
members.doc: Adds a new sub-path with one arc segment that consists of the arc that follows the edge of the oval bounded by the given rectangle, from startAngle radians around the oval up to startAngle + sweepAngle radians around the oval, with zero radians being the point on the right han...

members.name: addPolygon
members.doc: Adds a new sub-path with a sequence of line segments that connect the given points.

members.name: addRRect
members.doc: Adds a new sub-path that consists of the straight lines and curves needed to form the rounded rectangle described by the argument.

members.name: addRSuperellipse
members.doc: Adds a new sub-path that consists of curves needed to form the rounded superellipse described by the argument.

members.name: addPath
members.doc: Adds the sub-paths of `path`, offset by `offset`, to this path.

members.name: extendWithPath
members.doc: Adds the sub-paths of `path`, offset by `offset`, to this path. The current sub-path is extended with the first sub-path of `path`, connecting them with a lineTo if necessary.

members.name: close
members.doc: Closes the last sub-path, as if a straight line had been drawn from the current point to the first point of the sub-path.

members.name: reset
members.doc: Clears the Path object of all sub-paths, returning it to the same state it had when it was created. The _current point_ is reset to the origin.

members.name: contains
members.doc: Tests to see if the given point is within the path. (That is, whether the point would be in the visible portion of the path if the path was used with Canvas.clipPath.)

members.name: shift
members.doc: Returns a copy of the path with all the segments of every sub-path translated by the given offset.

members.name: transform
members.doc: Returns a copy of the path with all the segments of every sub-path transformed by the given matrix.

members.name: getBounds
members.doc: Computes the bounding rectangle for this path.

members.name: combine
members.doc: Combines the two paths according to the manner specified by the given `operation`.

members.name: computeMetrics
members.doc: Creates a PathMetrics object for this path, which can describe various properties about the contours of the path.

members.doc: Called for every tap down including every tap down that's part of a double click or a long press, except touches that include enough movement to not qualify as taps (e.g. pans and flings).

members.name: onForcePressStart
members.doc: Called when a pointer has tapped down and the force of the pointer has just become greater than ForcePressGestureRecognizer.startPressure.

members.name: onForcePressEnd
members.doc: Called when a pointer that had previously triggered onForcePressStart is lifted off the screen.

members.name: onSecondaryTap
members.doc: Called for a tap event with the secondary mouse button.

members.doc: Called for a tap down event with the secondary mouse button.

members.name: onSingleTapUp
members.doc: Called for the first tap in a series of taps, consecutive taps do not call this method.

members.name: onSingleTapCancel
members.doc: Called for each touch that becomes recognized as a gesture that is not a short tap, such as a long tap or drag. It is called at the moment when another gesture from the touch is recognized.

members.name: onUserTap
members.doc: Called for the first tap in a series of taps when onUserTapAlwaysCalled is disabled, which is the default behavior.

members.name: onSingleLongTapStart
members.doc: Called for a single long tap that's sustained for longer than kLongPressTimeout but not necessarily lifted. Not called for a double-tap-hold, which calls onDoubleTapDown instead.

members.name: onSingleLongTapMoveUpdate
members.doc: Called after onSingleLongTapStart when the pointer is dragged.

members.name: onSingleLongTapEnd
members.doc: Called after onSingleLongTapStart when the pointer is lifted.

members.name: onSingleLongTapCancel
members.doc: Called after onSingleLongTapStart when the pointer is canceled.

members.name: onDoubleTapDown
members.doc: Called after a momentary hold or a short tap that is close in space and time (within kDoubleTapTimeout) to a previous short tap.

members.name: onTripleTapDown
members.doc: Called after a momentary hold or a short tap that is close in space and time (within kDoubleTapTimeout) to a previous double-tap.

members.name: onDragSelectionUpdate
members.doc: Called repeatedly as a mouse moves while dragging.

members.name: onDragSelectionEnd
members.doc: Called when a mouse that was previously dragging is released.
